The crown above the throne, in encaustic painting, held a comely beardless image with flowing yellow hair. With a little of the breast covered by a scant cloth, above the spread wings of an eagle, which with head raised contemplated it fixedly. Which was wreathed with an azure diadem, adorned with seven rays; and at the eagle's feet a branch here and a branch there of green and undying laurel, and such signs, one to each side, were expressed. In the like manner I saw painted in every crown, that is, the figure proper to its planet.

It fell out by chance that behind my shoulders was the jewel holding the history of wing-footed Mercury; and, turning, I saw how his kindness was corrupted when he found himself in the malignant tail of the venomous Scorpion. And straightening again I thought how, in a most abject habit, I found myself among so many sumptuous garments — neither more nor less than that deadly beast, misshapen and vile among the most noble signs of the zodiac.

Then they sat in an ordered way upon the magnificent benches. Which went round the whole circuit of the walls. Now on the right side and the left of the court, as many as could aptly sit, the noble ladies most richly adorned, and with unusual and elegant dressings of the head, with womanly devices, their hair drawn back and plaited in distinct little knots, the fairest in the world. Some with the fair head curled in Poppaean ringlets, justly parted and modestly waved above the rosy and shining foreheads and the smooth temples. And others with hair (like obsidian, not of Latium, not of Spain, but of India) of the deepest black, comelily adorned with the whitest pearls, and with clasps of incredible price ornamented at their snowy shoulders.

They stood with so much reverence and attention that all at one time, when the servers at the tables made their reverences kneeling, these did the same, rising from their pleasant seats. Each clothed in shining gold, with marvellous weaving and workmanship. These did not eat at these tables.

Over against the triumphing Queen there answered the opening of the third curtain, which was a great and distinguished door, not of marble, but of lovely and hardest eastern jasper. Made by art and by ancient workmanship, very notable and worthy. On either side, here and there, of this

p. 103confidence: unstatedverified

excellentissima porta verso alle donne alla mensa sedente, demoravano le adolescentule musice, sette per lato, cum habiti Nymphei dignissimi et pretiosi. Le quale in omni mutatione, overo depositione dilla dapale mensa, variavano soni et gli instrumenti. Et dummentre si epulava, altre di queste cum angelico et Sireneo concento suavemente oscinavano. Hora in uno subito furono collocati tripodi di Hebeno, et temporarie mense, senza tumulto et strepito, ma ciascuna paratissima al suo destinato officio, et cum affectuoso conato aviduta et perspicace, et al suo iniuncto et imposito ministerio totalmente intenta.

Et quivi primariamente dinanti la Regina furono affermati tripodi di tale factura. Sopra una rotundatione di optimo diaspro, egregiamente liniato. Sopra el quale erano tre stipiti infixi. Lo imo degli quali desineva sopra il piano in una rapida branchia de leone d’oro, cum exquisita fogliatura gli styli ingurgitante, circuncirca investiti di politissima fogliatura. Et nel mediano suo ciascuno havea appacto uno capitulo di puppo, nel medio di due passe alette retinuto, dagli quali verso l’uno all’altro pandava uno fasciculo di rami coacervati nel medio turgescente, cum varii fructi referto. Gli quali styli nella suprema parte haveano una proiectura aptissima ad substinire la rotunda mensa dinanti a essa regina, questo instrumento era immutabile, ma le mense rotunde subitarie variavano. Come variava la materia degli vasi ad qualunque mutamento di mensa. Daposcia in uno battere di ochio, fue sopra questo tripodo posto una rotunda mensa d’oro aequatissima per diametro pedi tre et di crassitudine policaria et di questa forma et mensura erano tutti gli sequenti. Et sopra le eburnee mense fue explicato uno odoroso mantile di panno hormisino verde et politulamente distenso, lato et longo quasi fina sopra al pavimento, defilato nella extremitate per tutto, cum gli proprii fili ritorti, et commixti di fili aurei et argentei, dependuli sotto una lista, overo phrygio, di uno sextante la sua latitudine, et subtilmente ritramata, et di perle copiosamente fulcita. Dal pavimento suspesi aequabilmente uno palmo circuncirca per omni lato. Et di questo operamento tutti gli mantili erano

most excellent door, towards the ladies seated at the table, there stood the young musicians, seven to a side, in most worthy and precious nymphlike dress. Who, at every changing or clearing of the banquet table, varied their sounds and their instruments. And while the feast went on, others of these sang sweetly with an angelic and Siren-like harmony.

Now in an instant there were set out tripods of ebony, and tables for the time, without tumult or noise, but each server most ready for her appointed office, and eager and clear-sighted with an affectionate effort, and wholly intent upon the service enjoined and laid upon her.

And here first of all, before the Queen, tripods of such a making were set fast. Upon a rounding of the best jasper, distinguishedly lined. Above which were fixed three stems. The lowest part of which ended upon the flat in a swift lion's paw of gold, engulfing the shafts with exquisite foliage, and clothed round about with the most polished foliage. And in the middle of each was fitted a little boy's head, held in the midst of two spread wings, from which there hung, from the one towards the other, a little bundle of branches heaped together, swelling in the middle, filled with various fruits. Which shafts in their topmost part had a projection most apt to bear up the round table before the Queen. This framework was unchanging, but the sudden round tables varied. As the material of the vessels varied at every change of table.

Then in the blink of an eye there was set upon this tripod a round table of gold, most level, three feet in diameter and a thumb's breadth thick; and of this form and measure were all that followed. And upon the ivory tables was spread a scented cloth of green silk, neatly stretched out, broad and long almost down to the pavement, unravelled at the edge all round, with its own threads twisted and mingled with threads of gold and silver, hanging beneath a band, or border, a sixth of a foot in its breadth, subtly rewoven and richly furnished with pearls. Hung a hand's breadth clear of the pavement, evenly, all round on every side. And of this workmanship all the cloths were

p. 104confidence: unstatedverified

nelle sue extremitate phymbriati et decoramente ornati. Di proximo sequitoe una venusta et agile fanciulla cum una larga latina aurea colmata, di fiori di viole Amethistine lutheole et bianche, quale nella nova vera odorifere, per tutte le mense (excepta quella della Regina sempre nuda) promptissimamente disseminandole sparse. La Sacra maiestate della Regina exuto se havea il pomposo sagulo regillo, che tale mai non vide Lolia Paulina Romana, et ristoe in una sumptuosissima investitura belluata, di purpurante villito chermeo, per tutto contexto di multiplice avicule et altri animaletti, fronde et fiori, di nodatura ordinata, et alquanto le opere tumide di illustrissime margarite, cum uno tenuissimo suparo di sopra. Infecto uno pauculo di croceo colore sericeo propalando le coperte opere et il Chermeo per la sua lympica subtilitate. Il quale habito era in summo legiadro et venusto et Imperiale. Succedeteno poscia due elegante fanciulle. Le quale portorono una artificiosa fontana di continuo fundere, artificiosamente l’aqua reassumendo, che la spargeva, et era di nitido oro, in una concha bellissima operatura fundata, et anti di tutti la puoseron dinanti alla Regina. Et non più praesto sopra di l’aurea mensa fue appraesentata, che inseme legiadre inclinatione feceron, inclinando parimente la testa adornata. Et cum il genuflexo uno policari meno di agiungere al terso pavimento. Simigliante riverentie compositamente ad uno tempo le mediastime ministre che famulavano, successivamente observatrice et dinanti et daposcia all’offerire di qualunque cosa faceano, et ad la remotione. Tre altre praestante adulescentule appresso quelle sequitorono. Una cum uno aureo Gutturnio. Et l’altra cum uno bacile, overo malluvio lucentissimo. La tertia cum una delicata tovaglia di setta bianchissima.

La diva Regina le mano lavatose, quella gerula del aureo palubro riceveva la lotura, che nella fontana reassumpta non ritornasse. Et quella del gutturnio baiula, tanta aqua odorissima infundeva, quanto se effundeva, perché la fontana di miro excogitato non se vacuasse. La tertia agevola le mano tergeva. Il sparso et lato vaso di questa fontana, fondato fue artificiosamente sopra quatro rotule, et conducevano discurrendo sopra le mense ad lavare habilissimamente

fringed at their edges and seemly adorned.

Next there followed a comely and nimble girl with a wide golden vessel heaped with flowers of violets — amethyst-coloured, pale yellow and white, such as are fragrant in the new spring — which she most readily scattered and strewed over all the tables (except the Queen's, which was always bare).

The sacred majesty of the Queen had put off the pompous royal mantle, such as Lollia Paulina of Rome never saw, and remained in a most sumptuous figured garment of purple crimson pile, woven all over with manifold birds and other little animals, fronds and flowers, of an ordered knot-work, and the work somewhat swelling with the most illustrious pearls, with a very thin overgarment above. Tinged with a little of a saffron silken colour, showing through, by its clear thinness, the covered work and the crimson beneath. Which habit was in the highest degree graceful and comely and imperial.

Then there came two elegant girls. Who carried an artful fountain that poured continually, artfully taking up again the water that it scattered; and it was of shining gold, founded in a basin of most beautiful workmanship, and before all else they set it before the Queen. And no sooner was it presented upon the golden table than together they made a graceful bow, bending likewise their adorned heads. And kneeling within a thumb's breadth of reaching the burnished pavement. Like reverences, in an ordered way and at one time, the attendant servers who waited made — following one another, and observing them both before and after the offering of anything whatever, and at its removal.

Three other excellent young women followed after those. One with a golden ewer. And the other with a basin, or hand-bowl, most shining. The third with a delicate towel of the whitest silk.

The divine Queen having washed her hands, she that bore the golden bowl received the washing, so that it should not go back and be taken up again into the fountain. And she that carried the ewer poured in as much scented water as was poured out, so that the fountain of wonderful devising should not empty itself. The third lightly dried her hands.

The wide and spreading vessel of this fountain was artfully founded upon four little wheels, and they carried it running along over the tables to wash most aptly

p. 105confidence: unstatedverified

le mano di tutti gli discumbenti. Il quale nel medio promineva ultra gli sui lati labii di bulle gemmale inoculati, alveato compositamente, quale era la lacuna del vaso in circuito, et cum altri expressi. Sopra questa prominente parte assideva uno nobilissimo vaso et sopra ad questo uno altro variato, ma ambidui coniugati di due ansule, cum exquisita depolitura et elegante operatura et pretiosissima ornatura. Imperoché tra gli altri inextimabili gioielli nel propillato suo migrante in uno fiore, fora del quale emineva uno adamante deformato in uno pirulo cum l’aculeato nel fiore infixo per tutto collustrante, di invisa et inexcogitata granditudine. Et secondo il mio odorante senso, l’aqua iudicai di rose, immixto succo di cortice limonario et pauculo d’ambra, o vero di Beenzuvì cum solerte gradatione, cum grata et suave odorificatione.

In medio di questa stupenda area, fue exposito uno mirando vaso da suffumigio, non solamente per la nobile et perfecta materia, la quale era puro et optimo oro. Ma per la conspicua et antiquaria factura, cum l’Anteride sopra tre rapaci pedi di foeda Harpyia. I quali in fogliatura praestavano illigamento ad essa basi triangulare, di historiette copiosamente ornata, secondo che tale metallo expostula. Sopra gli porrecti angoli degli quali, tre spiritelli nudi assistevano, ordinatamente constituti, alti di dui cubiti, cum le scapulete volute l’una ad l’altra, convicini l’uno cum l’altro. Calcavano la basi nel angulo pausando cum il dextro pede, et cum l’altro pensile et soluto, verso il firmato dell’altro Puello. Et ciascuno ambidui gli cubiti sublevati, tenivano uno stylo balausticato, et nel imo gracile, et nella parte superiore fatiscente in una conchula per omni mane, dilatata nella apertione, et poco lacunata, cum gli oruli lati. Sei erano cum debita circuitione, uno al altro adhaerentise. Tra lo interscapilio degli alati Puelluli dal centrico puncto della piana della dicta basi triangulare, ascendeva uno stylo di egregio expresso di candelabro antico, il quale nel suo acuminato teniva la sua conchula, quale l’antedicte, et di tanta apertura, quanta conveniva ad occupatione dil vacuo, tra le sei conchule mediano relicto. Le quali conchule havevano le ministre g

the hands of all who sat at meat. Which in the middle stood out beyond its own lips, set with studs of gems, seemly channelled, as was the hollow of the vessel round about, and with other expressions.

Upon this projecting part sat a most noble vessel, and above this another of a different kind, but both joined by two little handles, with an exquisite polishing and elegant workmanship and most precious ornament. For among the other inestimable jewels, in its cover passing into a flower, out of which there rose a diamond shaped into a little pear, with its point fixed in the flower, shining all over, of an unheard-of and unimaginable size. And by my sense of smell I judged the water to be of roses, mixed with the juice of lemon rind and a little amber, or benzoin, in a skilful gradation, with a welcome and sweet scenting.

In the middle of this stupendous space there was set out a wonderful vessel for perfuming, not only for its noble and perfect material, which was pure and best gold, but for its notable and antique making; with its support upon three rapacious feet of a foul harpy. Which, in foliage, gave a binding to that triangular base, plentifully adorned with little histories, as such a metal demands.

Upon the outstretched corners of which three naked spirits stood, set in order, two cubits high, with their little shoulders turned one towards another, near one to another. They trod upon the base, resting at the corner with the right foot, and with the other hanging and free, towards the fixed foot of the next boy. And each of them, both elbows raised, held a shaft in the form of a pomegranate flower, slender at the bottom, and in the upper part opening into a little shell for every hand, widened at the mouth and a little hollowed, with broad rims. Six there were in a due circuit, cleaving one to another.

Between the shoulders of the winged boys, from the central point of the flat of the said triangular base, there rose a shaft of distinguished expression of an antique candelabrum, which at its point held its little shell, like those aforesaid, and of as great an opening as suited to fill the empty space left in the middle between the six shells. Which shells the servers had

p. 106confidence: unstatedverified

complete di accense prune, et di cenere poscia ricoperte, et di sopra la cinere bulliva una ampulla aurea per qualunque conchula. Cum dissimile liquore, o vero aque cum infusione diurna delle materie odorose, come suspicai, che ciascuna ampulla havesse distincta aqua, quale se potria dire in una aqua Rosacea, Narancea, Myrtea. Di fronde tenelle di lauro, di fiori sambuculi et altre notissime, cum variata et sotiale materia odorante, et queste bulliendo una inexperta fragrantia spirava per tutto suavissima. Alla praesentia della magnificentissima Regina sempre famulavano tre venerante et comptule puelle cum politione degli velanti habiti di oro et di seta miro modo tessuti. Il colore all’intuito gratiosamente cangiante, del coloramento degli mantili, che cusì come si mutava gli mantili, per il modo medesimo di vestimenti Nymphei le ministrante quanto al colore se variavano, cum uno lepidissimo grumo degli drapi sotto la sua stricta cinctura, gyrando dalle carnose et nivee spalle, et tirati sopra il copioso pecto moderatamente tumido, ad exprimere la vallecula mammillare, tanto extremamente voluptica, che lo optatissimo alimento ad gli speculanti parco rendeva, cum mille torquetti et cordelle d’oro et di seta comptule ornato. Di cura studiosa foeminile, ad praecipitante voluptate, degli illecti et amorosi sguardi, dolcissimo saporamento, superante qualunque cibato appectibile et gratioso, calciate di calciamini d’oro cum lunaria apertione sopra il nudo pede tutte parimente cum fibule auree volupticamente nexe. Cum defluo capillamento biondo et uberrimo et fina alle sure distenso. Nella bianchissima fronte cincti di strophiole di grosse et uniforme margerite. Assistevano esse trine ante essa cum singulare et divota riverentia, molto accorte et ad tale officio disposite cum praecipuo et prompto ministerio, le quale non servivano, se non ad una mensa. Sopra venendo poscia l’altra mutatione di mensa, tutte queste ristavano in pedi serve facte cum le ulne nodate cum summa veneratione. Et cusì successive tutte le altre observavano, sempre altre tante in numero innovavase. Delle tre ministrante a ciascuno convivante. Quella tra le due, il cibo offeriva, quella da lato dextro assotiava di sotto quel cibo cum una platineta, a ciò che cosa alcuna altronde non cadesse. La tertia alla parte leva elegantemente gli labra tergeva cum uno candidissimo tersorio subtile et mundissimo. Ad qualunque acto in prompto era la riverentia. Il tersorio più non era reiterato a quello officio. Ma proiecto dalla damigella nel pavimento, era repente dalle astante collecto et d’indi asportato. Et quanti morsi dovevasi porgere, tanti odoranti et profumigati tersorii plicati, seco apportavano mutatorii seritii, cum mirifica operatura textili. A ciascuno dunque degli discumbenti tale ordine della mensa diligentemente

filled with kindled embers, and covered over then with ash; and above the ash there boiled a golden flask for each shell. With a different liquor, or waters with a day's infusion of scented matter — as I guessed, that each flask had its own distinct water, such as one might call rose-water, orange-water, myrtle-water; of tender laurel fronds, of elder flowers and others well known, with a varied and sociable scented matter. And these, boiling, breathed everywhere a most sweet and unknown fragrance.

In the presence of the most magnificent Queen there always waited three reverent and neat girls, with the trimness of veiling garments of gold and silk woven in a wonderful manner. The colour graciously changing to the eye, of the colouring of the table-cloths, so that as the cloths were changed, in the same manner the nymphlike garments of the servers were varied as to colour; with a most charming gathering of the drapery beneath their tight girdle, turning from their fleshy and snowy shoulders, and drawn over the full breast moderately swelling. Shod with golden shoes with a moon-shaped opening over the bare foot, all alike fastened with golden clasps. With flowing hair, blond and most abundant, and falling to their calves. On the whitest forehead girt with little fillets of great and uniform pearls.

These three stood before her with a singular and devout reverence, very heedful and set to such an office with a chief and ready service; who served at one table only. When afterwards the next change of table came, all these stood upon their feet, made servants with their arms folded in the utmost reverence. And thus in succession all the others observed it, and always as many again were renewed in number.

Of the three servers to each guest: the one between the two offered the food; she on the right side accompanied that food underneath with a little plate, so that nothing should fall elsewhere. The third, on the left, elegantly wiped the lips with a most white napkin, fine and cleanest. At every act the reverence was ready. The napkin was never used a second time for that office, but, thrown by the damsel upon the pavement, was at once gathered up by those standing by and carried thence away. And as many mouthfuls as were to be offered, so many scented and perfumed folded napkins they brought with them for changing, silken, of wonderful woven workmanship.

To each of those at table, then, such an order of service they diligently

p. 107confidence: unstatedverified

observavano. Imperoché conviva niuno ad tale pasto alcuna cosa attrectava, ma opportunamente era dalle servente pabulato, excepto del poculo. Alla primaria mensa da poscia tutti lavatose cum l’antedicto fonte di solerte artificio per violentia di concepto aere, o vero introcluso, saliva l’aqua reassumpta. La quale cosa tanto exquisita, pensitai che per gemine fistule de qui et de lì inaequale, per uno intersito pariete nel mediano pertusato era el vaso intro diviso, et per proprio impulso violentata l’aqua ascendeva, la quale havendo cum subtile investigato cognita extremamente grata mi fue. Dapò la lotione di tutti, alla Regina primo, et successivamente a ciascuno, dalle philocale puelle ministrante, fue dato uno volemo pomulo d’oro, egregiamente transforato, et introclusa una mixtura pastale di mirabile odoramento, per tale causa, che le ociose mano di qualunque dal dicto Trigone, o vero pila fusseron ad qualche acto occupate, et gli sensi ad riguardare et odorare, cum pretiosi lapilli decorata. Quivi dunque per omni mutatione di condimento, due domicelle edeatrice bellissimamente trahevano in la mediana della regia corte, uno stupendo repositorio sopra quatro labile rote, nella parte anteriore in forma di uno Naustibulo, o vero cymbio el residuo postero deformato in triumphante Carro di purgatissimo oro, cum efferato di multiplice Scylle et monstruli aquatici, et molti exquisitissimi expressi, et mirificamente exacti, di richissimi lapilli cum elegante distributione et mirifico ornamento, per tutto compositamente referto, il scintillare degli quali per tutto il susceptibile ambito splendevano, et nel rutilare degli altri gioielli in omni lato diversamente locati cum fulguratione ricontrantise, diresti licentemente ivi Phoebo le splendente come comente, cum una Nympha sedente, il volto cui non meno cum gli ochii illustre venustava. Dunque alla continua nitentia, et splendore di tante ineffabile operature, additamento ritrovare non si potrebbe, né aequivalente comparatione quantunque si fusse il Babylonio Tempio cum le tre auree statue. Intro del quale erano capacemente praeparate tutte cose Embammate et caryciamenti opportune ad tutta la exigentia della variata mensa, portava mantili, fiori, calici, tersorii, vasi, fussinule, poculenti, esculenti, et saporamenti. Questa plaustraria Nympha poscia il praeparamento alle diruitrice promptuariamente distribuiva. Deponentisi poscia la mensa per l’altra mutatione, omni cosa sopra recitata alla diruitoria rheda ritornava. La quale partitose, le fanciulle tubante di tube ductrice, quale non furono invente da Piseo Therreno, né da g ii

kept. For no guest at such a meal touched anything, but was fed in due time by the servers, save for the cup.

At the first table, afterwards, all having washed at the aforesaid fountain of skilful artifice — by the force of gathered, or enclosed, air the water rose and was taken up again. Which thing being so exquisite, I thought that by twin pipes, here and there unequal, through a wall set between, pierced in the middle, the vessel was divided within, and by its own impulse the forced water ascended; which, having learnt by a subtle examination, was extremely pleasing to me.

After the washing of all, to the Queen first and thereafter to each in turn, the beauty-loving serving girls gave a golden apple, distinguishedly pierced through, and enclosing a paste of a wonderful scenting — for this cause, that the idle hands of each should be occupied with some act by the said ball, and the senses in looking and smelling; and it was adorned with precious little stones.

Here, then, at every change of dishes, two damsel stewards drew most beautifully into the middle of the royal court a stupendous store-carriage upon four running wheels, in its forward part in the form of a boat, or skiff, the hinder remainder shaped into a triumphal car of the purest gold, wrought fiercely with manifold Scyllas and little water-monsters, and many most exquisite expressions, and wonderfully finished, with richest little stones in an elegant distribution and wonderful ornament, filled seemlily throughout — the sparkling of which shone through all the space that could receive it, and meeting in a flashing with the glowing of the other jewels set variously on every side, you would freely say that Phoebus was there with his shining locks, with a Nymph sitting, whose face made her no less lovely with her shining eyes. So that, for the continual brightness and splendour of so many unspeakable workmanships, no addition could be found, nor any equivalent comparison, were it even the Babylonian temple with its three golden statues.

Within which were amply prepared all sauces and seasonings needful for the whole requirement of the varied table; it carried cloths, flowers, cups, napkins, vessels, little forks, drink, food and seasonings. This waggon Nymph then readily distributed the preparation to those who cleared away.

The table being then taken down for the next change, everything above recited returned to the clearing carriage. And when it had departed, the girls with the leading trumpets — such as were invented neither by Piseus the Tyrrhenian, nor by

p. 108confidence: unstatedverified

Maleto re di Etruria et inseme le Tibicinarie immediate inchoavano a sonare, et per questo observato modo omni fiata faceano, che il gestatorio se dispartiva. Sonando dummentre che quella ritornasse, poscia cessavano. Et quando si mutava la mensa, et queste variavano gli musicali instrumenti, et quando cessavano, alhora le cantatrice dolcissimamente cantavano, da fare sopire le Sirene, cum Aeolio modulo, cum Tibie Aulitice, et Bifore, del quale modo inventore non fue Troezenio Dardanio. Et per questo ordinato modo continuamente si udivano gratissimi soni, si auscultava lepidissimi concenti, si persentiva delectabile melodia, iocundissimo odoramento, se exhauriva, et lautissima satietate suavissimamente gustando si receveva. Omni cosa dunque mutuamente ad dignitate, ad gratia et oblectamento sencia difecto convenivano. Ad questa primaria et splendida mensa, tutti gli mensali utensilii, o vero instrumenti furono di finissimo oro, et di questo la tabula rotunda dinanti la Regina. Et fue appraesentata una cordiale confectione, quanto io accuratamente coniecturare valeva, era una opifera compositione et praeoptima, di rasura corni cioè de unicornio, cum gli dui sandali, Margarite trite nell’aqua ardente al foco ignite, et in quella extincte fina all’ultimo recisamento, Manna, Nuclei Pinei et aqua rosacea, mosco, oro macinato molto pretiosamente composito et ponderato, et cum finissimo Zacharo et amylo streto in morselli. Di questo ne dette due prehense cum moderato intervallo, et sencia potione per ciascuno, cibo di prohibire omni obstinata febre, et excludere qualunque trista lassitudine. Facto questo in instante furono levate et rimote tutte cose et sparse le olente viole in terra et denudata la mensa. Diqué non più praesto che cusì facto fue, che di novo un’altra fiata fue ricoperta la mensa di Talasicho panno, et etiam tutte le ministre, et come in la prima la coprirono di fiori cedrini, Narancei, et di Limoni odorissimi. Et quivi appresentorono in vasi di Beryllo, et di questa gemma era la mensa regia (excepte le fussinule, che erano d’oro) cinque offule, o vero frictille, di pastamento crocato et cum fervente aqua rosea et Zacharo immassate, iterum et cum aspergine della dicta aqua moscata finissima irrorate, pruinate et di subtilissimo Zacharo. Questi tali globuli di tanta suave degustatione et diversificata, furono diligentemente cocti cum tale distinctione. La prima offerta, in olio di fiori narancei. La seconda, in olio di chariophylli. La tertia, in olio di fiori di Gausamino, la quarta, in olio di finissimo beenzuì, l’ultima, in olio expresso di mosco et di ambra. Havendo nui saporosamente et cum avida et cum lurca appetentia questo delectabile edulio degustato, appraesentorono uno solemne calice poscia, della petra sopra nominata,

Maletus king of Etruria — and with them the flute-players immediately began to play; and in this observed manner they did every time that the carriage went away. Playing while it returned; then they ceased. And when the table was changed, these too varied their musical instruments; and when they ceased, then the singers sang most sweetly, enough to put the Sirens to sleep, in the Aeolian mode, with hautboys and double flutes, of which mode Dardanius of Troezen was not the inventor.

And in this ordered manner there were continually heard most welcome sounds, most charming harmonies were listened to, delightful melody was felt, a most joyful scenting was drawn in, and a most splendid fullness was received, tasting most sweetly. Everything, then, agreed mutually in dignity, in grace and in delight, without any defect.

At this first and splendid table all the table utensils, or instruments, were of the finest gold, and of this the round table before the Queen. And there was presented a cordial confection: as far as I was able to conjecture accurately, it was a helpful and most excellent composition of shaved horn — that is, of unicorn — with the two sandalwoods; pearls ground in burning water kindled at the fire, and quenched in it down to the last cutting; manna, pine kernels and rose-water, musk, ground gold, very preciously composed and weighed, and pressed into morsels with the finest sugar and starch. Of this she gave two takings, at a moderate interval, and without drink, to each — a food to forbid every obstinate fever, and to shut out any sad weariness.

This done, in an instant all things were taken up and removed, and the fragrant violets scattered on the ground, and the table stripped bare. And no sooner was this so done than once again the table was covered with sea-purple cloth, and likewise all the servers; and as at the first they covered it with flowers of citron, orange and most fragrant lemon.

And here they presented, in vessels of beryl — and of this gem was the royal table (except the little forks, which were of gold) — five little cakes, or fritters, of a saffron paste kneaded with hot rose-water and sugar, and again sprinkled with a shower of the said finest musked water, frosted over with the finest sugar. These little globes, of so sweet and varied a tasting, were diligently cooked with this distinction: the first offering in oil of orange flowers; the second in oil of cloves; the third in oil of jasmine flowers; the fourth in oil of the finest benzoin; the last in oil pressed of musk and amber. Having tasted this delectable dish savourily and with an eager and greedy appetite, they then presented a solemn cup of the stone named above,

p. 109confidence: unstatedverified

cum il copertorio suo, et di sopra ancora, de uno tenuissimo velamine sericeo vermiculatamente ritramato, di seta et di oro tecto, et sopra la spalla della baiulante reiecto, et al dorso parte dependulo. Et cum questa observantia tutti gli vasculi poculatorii et condimentorii contecti appraesentavano. Dentro al quale bibatorio havevano infuso uno pretiosissimo vino, unde sencia fallire enucleatamente suspicai, esso dio negli Elysii campi vindemiando havere posto la sua divinitate in tanto suavissimo liquamine. Ceda quivi dunque il vino Thasio, et qualunque pretioso haustibile. Sencia differire, dopo la gratissima potione deposita questa mensa lautissima. Et sopra il lustrante pavimento sparsi gli odorosi fiori, uno mantile fue praestamente extenso di panno di seta muriceo, et di carnee, o vero molochine rose, candide, vermiglie, moschete, damascene, tetraphylle, et Giebbedine di sopra commixte disseminorono. Et expeditamente portorono le nove famulatrice, del dicto panno et coloramento indute, sei incisure per ciascuno di capo caecamente saginato, et humidamente cum la perfusa pinguitie sua et aqua rosea crocata asperso, et cum succamine Neranceo commixto, optimamente assato et tutto poscia inaurato, et cum sei accommodate scindule di niveo pane Mnestorense, dinanti depositorono. Et appresso cum saporamento di succo Limonario cum fino Zacharo modificato, cum seme di pine et cum il suo hepate macinato, adiuncto aqua rosacea, mosco et croco et Cinamomo electo, et cusì tutti gli saporamini cum praecipua et exquisita gradatione compositi et participati et optimamente conditi. Gli vasi tutti furono di Topatio et la rotunda mensa. Questa tertia frugale et magnifica mensa, come di sopra dispreparata, fue sencia mora l’altra innovata, et cum sericio panno de raso di colore luteo lucidulo ricoperta (et le servitrice indute del medesimo) et di fragranti fiori di lilii convallii et di Narcyso tutto florulato, immediate fue tale condimento exposito, septe bolli di polpa di perdice cum acre diligentia iurulenta, tosta, et altretante bucelle di oculato et lacteo pane. Saporamento. Accere, mandole macinate cum tricocto Zacharo, amylo, sandalo citrino, mosco et aqua rosea. Vasi di Chrysolitho, et la circulare mensa. Ultimo offerivano il pretiosissimo poculo, et cusì observato era nelle sequente. Rimota la quarta opima mensa, nella quinta fue revestita la tavola di panno di seta Phoeniceo, similmente era lo habito Nymphale. Fiori cairi, lutei, candidi, et amethistihi. Pulmento octo morselli di polpamento g iii

with its cover, and above it besides a most thin silken veil rewoven in fine work, covered with silk and gold, and thrown back over the shoulder of her that bore it, and hanging partly down her back. And with this observance they presented all the little vessels for drinking and for seasoning, covered over. Within which drinking-cup they had poured a most precious wine, whence without failing I plainly suspected that the god himself, vintaging in the Elysian fields, had put his divinity into so sweet a liquor. Let the Thasian wine yield here, then, and every precious thing that may be drunk.

Without delay, after the most welcome draught, this splendid table was taken down. And, the fragrant flowers being scattered upon the shining pavement, a cloth was readily stretched out of purple silk cloth; and they strewed over it flesh-coloured, or mallow-pink, roses, white, vermilion, musk, damascene, four-petalled and Ghiebbedine, mingled.

And promptly the nine servers, clothed in the said cloth and colouring, set down before each of us six cuttings of a blindly fattened head, moistened and sprinkled with its own poured fat and saffroned rose-water, and mixed with orange juice, excellently roasted and then all gilded over, and with six fitting slices of snowy Mnestorian bread. And thereafter with a seasoning of lemon juice tempered with fine sugar, with pine seeds and with its liver ground, adding rose-water, musk and saffron and choice cinnamon; and thus all the seasonings composed with a chief and exquisite gradation, shared out and excellently seasoned. All the vessels were of topaz, and the round table.

This third frugal and magnificent table being, as above, unprepared, without delay the next was renewed and covered with a silken cloth of satin of a bright yellow colour (and the servers clothed in the same), and all flowered with fragrant flowers of lilies of the valley and of narcissus. Immediately such a dish was set out: seven balls of partridge flesh with a sharp diligence, in broth, toasted, and as many mouthfuls of eyed and milky bread. Seasoning: maple-sap, almonds ground with thrice-boiled sugar, starch, citron sandalwood, musk and rose-water. Vessels of chrysolite, and the circular table. Last they offered the most precious cup, and thus it was observed in those that followed.

The fourth rich table being removed, at the fifth the board was clothed again with cloth of purple silk; and like was the nymphlike dress. Flowers dark, yellow, white and amethyst. For meat, eight morsels of the flesh

p. 110confidence: unstatedverified

di fasiano offertissimo et succido assato, et altretanti buccei di leve et candidissimo pane, saporio tale. Torli recenti cum pinuli, aqua narancea, succo granateo, Saccaro Colosino, et cinnamomo. Vasi di Smaragdo, et la mensa della sublime Regina. Asportata questa solenne mutatione, sencia intercalare, fue extenso uno panno di seta Ianthino, et gli Nymphei indumenti. Fiori le tre sorte di Iosamino, punicei, gialli et bianchi. Cibato bucconi nove dal carinato del conservabile Pavone cohumidamente iurulento et torrido adipato. Salsamento verdissimo et acidulo, cum pistachii triti, Saccaro Cyprico, amylo, mosco, Thymo, serpillo, origano biancho, et piperea. Vasi di Saphiro Cyaneo, et la mensa regale. Ad questa septima opipera mutatione, asportorono la sumptuosa tavola, tutta di bianchissimo eboro subtilmente segmentata, et riportata un’altra di pretioso ligno Aloè optimamente di glutino compacta, et da una extremitate all’altra, cum miro excogitato excavata di nobilissimi nodamenti di fogliatura fiori vasi, monstriculi et aviculette, et refarcita di nigro pastamento di mosco et ambra cum federata mixtura. Questo dritamente istimai elegantissima et cosa sumptuosa, odore spirante delectabile il mantile bianchissimo et subtile, cum vermicularia textura di Bysso di Carysto, et di tale panno gli ornati vestimenti delle fanciulle ministrante. Fiori di Cyclaminos, cum tutte maniere di Gariophylli excessivamente odorigeri. Dunque, chiunque valeria tanta suavissima et varia fragrantia cum continuo et novo congresso iocundissimo al senso considerare, non auso exprimere. Optima confectione in morselli, polpe di dactyli, cum pistachii, cum aqua di rose contriti, et Saccaro insulare, mosco, adulterata di oro pretioso trito, in tanto che le prehense tutte di oro appariano, tre per ciascuno furono date. Gli vasi di hiacyntho, et la mensa circulare, conveniente petra ad tanta excellentissima dispositione della diva mensa et lauticia, non subdita alla legie Licinia. Dapò la iocunda et gratissima degustatione di questa mirabile confectione, et ad terra gli fiori rivoluti, per una basilica magnificentia, fue sencia mora portata una grande concha aurea, et di prune accense piena, nella quale il mantile proiecto et gli tersorii di Bysso, tanto spatio elle nel foco il lasciorono, che tutto ignito si accense, et d’indi poscia educto et frigerato, se vide illaeso praepurato et mundissimo, come inanti. Et questa ancora fue una praeclara ostentatione et invisitata. Novissimamente gli tripodi et le tavole furono praestamente depositi, et d’indi asportati. Le quale tutte praeexcellentissime ostensione, quanto più pensiculatamente

of pheasant, most freely offered, roasted in its juices, and as many mouthfuls of light and whitest bread; the sauce such: fresh yolks with little pine kernels, orange-water, pomegranate juice, sugar of Colossae, and cinnamon. Vessels of emerald, and the table of the lofty Queen.

This solemn change being carried away, without any interval a cloth of violet silk was spread, and the nymphlike garments likewise. For flowers, the three kinds of jasmine, crimson, yellow and white. For food, nine mouthfuls from the breast of the ever-keeping peacock, moist in its broth and roasted in its fat. A sauce greenest and somewhat sharp, with pistachios ground, Cyprian sugar, starch, musk, thyme, wild thyme, white oregano, and pepper. Vessels of dark blue sapphire, and the royal table.

At this seventh sumptuous change they carried away the sumptuous board, all of the whitest ivory subtly inlaid, and brought back another of precious aloe wood, excellently compacted with glue, and from one end to the other hollowed with a wonderful devising into most noble knot-works of foliage, flowers, vessels, little monsters and small birds, and filled in with a black paste of musk and amber in a confederate mixture. This I rightly judged a most elegant and sumptuous thing, breathing a delightful scent; the cloth whitest and fine, with a fine-wrought weaving of byssus of Carystus, and of such cloth the adorned garments of the serving girls. Flowers of cyclamen, with all manners of gillyflowers exceedingly fragrant. So that whoever might be able to consider so sweet and various a fragrance, with its continual and new meeting most joyful to the sense, I do not dare to express.

An excellent confection in morsels: pulp of dates with pistachios, ground with rose-water, and island sugar, musk, adulterated with precious ground gold, so much that all the takings appeared of gold; three to each were given. The vessels of jacinth, and the circular table — a stone fitting to so excellent an ordering of the divine board and its splendour, not subject to the Licinian law.

After the joyful and most welcome tasting of this marvellous confection, and the flowers rolled to the ground, by a royal magnificence there was brought without delay a great golden basin full of kindled embers, into which the cloth was thrown and the napkins of byssus; and so long a space they left them in the fire that all was kindled and glowing, and thence drawn out and cooled, it was seen unhurt, purified and cleanest, as before. And this too was a distinguished and unheard-of showing. Last of all the tripods and the boards were readily taken down and carried thence away.

All which most excellent showings, the more carefully

p. 111confidence: unstatedverified

le considerava tanto più inscio stava et stupefacto, ma per certo sopra omni, cosa cum intensa admiratione prehendeva extremo oblectamento, videndo tante, et sì magne, et triumphante, et effusissime sumptuositate de incredibile impensa et lautitia, che meglio arbitro essere il tacere, che exiguamente dire, si non che di minimo pretio ceda quivi le Sicule dape, gli ornamenti Attalici, et gli vasi Corinthii, et le delitie Cyprie, et le saliare cene. Niente dimeno tanta suprema et excessiva alacritate et cordiale delectatione, et summa (in tante delitie) et extrema voluptate per una di queste tre, che a questa mutatione per sorte dinanti a me ministravano, mi era interrotta, intercepta, et contaminata, la quale havea quasi in tutto il venusto sembiante et repraesentativo aspecto dolcissimo di Polia, et in gesti excitanti, subduli et furacissimi risguardi. Questo ad me accedeva non pusillo incremento di suavitate, ad la summa et praecipua dulcitudine, degli saturativi et opimi condimenti, et largissima refectione. Ma pur acconciamente et sedulo gli ochii mei excitati, et illecti ritraheva, di mirare tante pretiosissime gemme, per tutto universalmente cum fulguritio illustramine praelucentissime, tanta diversitate de invise bellecie, Conspicui decoramenti, et quasi in chostei e’ gli havea mancipati, cum immoderata cupidine di spectare la correspondentia di quella summa pulchritudine. Finalmente per l’ordine praefato, le mense desordinate, me feceron nuto, che di loco me movere non dovesse, per le sequente pemmate, et richissimi et dulcissimi bellarii. Et quivi primo alla venerabile et diva praesentia della Regina, et subsequente poscia ad nui, Cinque formose famulante vestite di investitura di seta Cyanea et di aurea trama bellissime contexta, a ciascuno cum singulare praestantia inseme ad uno tempo sa ppraesentorono. La media all’altre teniva uno insolente arbusculo di cinabarissimo coralio, quale non sa trovarebbe alle Orchade insule di uno cubito alto. Sopra uno monticulo tutto di smaragdo superstitiosamente infixo. Il quale monticello iaceva sopra lo orificio di uno antiquario vaso di purgatissimo oro, quasi ad la similitudine di uno calice, alto altretanto, quanto il monticulo et il ramicoso coralio, pieno di miraveglioso artificio de frondato, non di nostra aetate expresso. Tra il gracilamento dil pede et dil calatho, nodava cum maxima politura uno pomulo di inextimabile factura, similmente la basi et la cupa erano di egregia anaglyphia di foglie, monstriculi et biforme scyllule tanto exquisitamente expressi, quanto mai Toreuma si potesse efferare, cum proportionata circulatione. Et il mordicante claustro dil monticulo glandulato era di incomparabili gioielli, et cusì per tutta la basi, ove g iiii

I considered them, the more ignorant and astonished I stood; but certainly above all things I took an extreme delight, with an intense admiration, seeing so many and so great and triumphing and most lavish sumptuosities of incredible cost and splendour, that I judge it better to be silent than to say too little of it — save that at the least price there yield here the Sicilian feasts, the ornaments of Attalus, and the Corinthian vessels, and the delights of Cyprus, and the Salian suppers.

Nevertheless so supreme and excessive a cheerfulness and heartfelt delight, and the utmost (among such delights) and extreme pleasure, was interrupted, intercepted and stained for me by one of these three who at this change happened to serve before me: who had almost wholly the comely semblance and the sweetest representing aspect of Polia, and in her stirring gestures, sly and most thievish glances. This brought me no small increase of sweetness to the highest and chief sweetness of the filling and rich seasonings and the most bountiful refreshment. But yet fittingly and carefully I drew back my eyes, stirred and enticed as they were, from beholding so many most precious gems, everywhere and universally shining with a flashing brightness, and such a diversity of unseen beauties and notable adornments — and had as it were made them her bondmen, with an immoderate longing to behold the answering of that highest beauty.

At last, in the order aforesaid, the tables being cleared, they made me a sign that I should not move from my place, for the sweetmeats that followed and the richest and sweetest dainties.

And here first to the venerable and divine presence of the Queen, and thereafter to us, five shapely servers, clothed in a garment of dark blue silk most beautifully woven with a golden thread, presented themselves together at one time to each with a singular excellence. She in the middle of the others held an uncommon little tree of cinnabar-red coral, such as would not be found in the Orkney isles, a cubit high. Fixed with great care upon a little hill all of emerald. Which little hill lay upon the mouth of an antique vase of the purest gold, almost in the likeness of a chalice, as high as the little hill and the branching coral, full of marvellous artifice of foliage, not expressed in our age.

Between the slenderness of the foot and the bowl there was knotted with the greatest polish a little apple of inestimable making; likewise the base and the cup were of distinguished relief-work of leaves, little monsters and two-formed little Scyllas, as exquisitely expressed as ever chased work could be wrought fiercely, with a proportioned circling. And the biting setting of the acorned little hill was of incomparable jewels, and so throughout the base, where

p. 112confidence: unstatedverified

decentissimamente fue opportuno. Fulguriciamente collustravano collocati. Negli rami del quale arbusculo, erano artificiosamente applicati alcuni floruli aperti, deformati in pentaphylla rosa. Alcuni di praelucente Saphyro, et tali di illustrante hiacyntho, o vero berilo. In cinque di questi fiori, dentro erano appacti, cinque pomuli, quanto una sorba et più, et di quella pictura, in uno apiceo aculeo d’oro, che promineva dal centro del fiore, mentivano illo producti.

La quale iuvencula riverente geniculata a terra, cum il dextro genochio, l’altro riservando levato, sopra esso acconciamente questo spectando Coralio reteniva. Il quale ancora oltra gli ramuli occupati degli pretiosi fiori, haveva nelle cime degli altri curiosamente infixe monstruose perle. Un’altra di queste haveva il poculo, cum pretioso liquore, quale non dede la superba Cleopatra al capitanio romano. Le tre altre exequivano il suo incumbente ministerio, come di sopra consueto. Extirpato dunque uno dopo l’altro, cum il bidentulo d’oro quelli fructuli (a mi incogniti et mai visi) ad nui offerendogli, saporissime li gustassemo. Ma la inopinabile suavitate di gusto ch’io sentiti, non altramente, quale si nella gratiosa materia disiuncta, fusse l’ingresso della optata forma. Et quivi furono restituiti gli volemi pomi d’oro, recitati di sopra. Novissimamente apparve una miraculosa opera, un’altra fontana perpetua per artifico excogitato della inanti dicta materia. Ma di altra dignissima deformatione et figmento, mirificamente tudiculata. Fundata sopra uno stabile Axide, per il quale le volubile rote invertivano. Sopra il quale Axide firmata constava una inaequale quadratratura tripedale longa,

it was most seemly and fitting. Placed there, they shone with a flashing light.

In the branches of which little tree there were artfully set certain open flowerets, shaped into a five-petalled rose. Some of shining sapphire, and some of bright jacinth, or beryl. In five of these flowers there were fitted within five little apples, as big as a sorb-apple and more, and of that same painting, upon a pointed golden spike that stood out from the centre of the flower, so that they feigned to have been produced there.

Which young girl, reverent and kneeling to the ground with her right knee, keeping the other raised, held this notable coral fitly upon it. Which, besides the little branches taken up by the precious flowers, had at the tips of the others monstrous pearls curiously fixed.

Another of these had the cup, with a precious liquor, such as proud Cleopatra did not give to the Roman captain. The three others carried out the service lying upon them, as customary above. Plucking off, then, one after another with the little golden fork those small fruits (unknown to me, and never seen), and offering them to us, we tasted them most savourily. But the unthinkable sweetness of taste that I felt was no otherwise than as if in the gracious matter, set apart, there were the entering in of the longed-for form. And here were given back the round golden apples recited above.

Last of all there appeared a miraculous work, another perpetual fountain by a devised artifice of the material named before. But of another most worthy shaping and figure, wonderfully wrought. Founded upon a fixed axle, by which the turning wheels went round. Upon which axle there stood, made fast, an unequal square three feet long,

p. 113confidence: unstatedverified

et lata bipedale, et triente sublevata. Nelle parte angulare per ciascuna sedeva una Harpyia, cum ambe l’ale alla corpulentia d’uno superiore vaso porrecte, superassidente, nel aequato mediano di questa quadrangula, cum gulule et undicule, et follicule coronicata optimamente alle extremitate circumvestita. Et in qualunque facia sua, per tertio divisa, la partitione mediana intersepta in undicule, contineva di semilevatura inscalpto uno triumpho di Satyri et di Nymphe cum Trophaei et exquisiti acti, excepte l’anteriore, et parte posteriore, moderatamente sinuate, le quale in lo loco de liniamento quadrato, se contineva una rotundatione interundulata, nella quale mirificamente era inscalpto uno sacrificulo, cum una veterrima ara in una et nell’altra cum pluscule figure et actione, gli residui vacui convicini, le caude delle Harpyie bifidate, et de qui et de lì aptissimamente in volubile fronde converse, egregiamente convestivano. Nel centro mediano dell’aequatura del narrato quadrangulo, fora di uno antiquario fogliamento, prosiliva uno veterrimo vaso bellissimo, la circuitione sua non excedente il contento dilla supposita quadrangulata piana. Et questo cum tutta la sequente opera, cum omni proportionata disquisitione et dell’ascenso, latitudine, et crassitudine, et cum decentissimi liniamenti vasarii, diligentissimamente delimato fue et perfinito, cum absoluta et depolita deformatione. Il quale nel suppresso orificio, nasceva una concha. L’ambito della quale excedeva il vaso basicale subiecto, cum canaliculi circumornata, et cum hiato sparso cum largi labri, quale mai Toreute valse cum la Tudicula tudiculare. Nel centrico puncto della quale, uno altro vaso promineva di incredibile factura mirando, nel tertio del imo del quale erano scindule tuberate extrinseco, poscia circuncingeva uno ordine de varie et inextimabile gemme umbiliculate, cum mutua alternatione del coloramento praefulgentissime adornato. Sopra questo appacto era uno monstrificato capo virile. Dal quale procedeva et de qui, et de lì la tectura sua in exquisita fogliatura, per tutto investiendo cum il congresso del opposito capo, decorando venustamente lo expedito corpo vaseo. Nella proiectura labrale sopra ad perpendiculo dil capo, assideva uno annulo, dal quale et de qui et de lì suspenso pendeva uno fasciculo cum acervati ramuli di fronde et fiori, et fructi, nel pandamento turgescente, cum praepolita illaqueatione, et in uno et in l’altro annulo. and two feet wide, and raised a third of a foot. In the corner parts there sat upon each a harpy, with both wings stretched out to the body of a vessel above, sitting over the levelled middle of this square, best clothed at the edges with a little cornice of gorges and wavings and husks.

And on each of its faces, divided into three, the middle partition, hedged between with wavings, held carved in half-relief a triumph of satyrs and of Nymphs with trophies and exquisite acts — except the front and the hinder part, moderately curved, which, in the place of a squared lineament, held a rounding waved within, in which was wonderfully carved a little sacrifice, with a most ancient altar in the one and in the other with several figures and actions; and the remaining empty places nearby the tails of the harpies, forked, and here and there most aptly turned into rolling fronds, distinguishedly clothed over.

In the middle centre of the level of the said square, out of an antique foliage, there sprang a most beautiful ancient vessel, its circuit not exceeding the compass of the square flat beneath it. And this, with all the work that follows, with every proportioned inquiry both of the rise, the breadth and the thickness, and with the most seemly lineaments of vessels, was most diligently filed and finished, with a perfect and polished shaping.

Which, at its pressed-in mouth, brought forth a basin. The circuit of which exceeded the base vessel beneath, adorned round about with little channels, and with a wide mouth and broad lips, such as no chaser ever had power to work with the graving tool.

At the central point of which another vessel stood out, wonderful for its incredible making; in the lower third of which were slices swelling on the outside, and then there girt it round an order of various and inestimable gems set like navels, most brilliantly adorned with a mutual alternation of the colouring. Above this was fitted a monstrous manly head. From which there went, here and there, its covering in exquisite foliage, clothing it all over at the meeting with the head opposite, beautifully adorning the free body of the vessel.

At the projection of the lip, perpendicular above the head, sat a ring, from which there hung, here and there, a little bundle with heaped-up small branches of fronds and flowers and fruits, swelling in its curve, with a well-polished knotting, both in the one ring and in the other.

little pipe through which flowed the water of the fountain, perpetual by artifice, into the basin beneath.

In the opening, then, of this vessel there stood out a most precious little hill, marvellously heaped of countless round gems pressed close one upon another, which with an unequal, or rough, shaping made the stony little hill most charmingly, with the flashing of various lightnings of colour, with a proportioned prominence.

At the top, or summit, of this little hill there grew a little tree of pomegranates, of trunk, or stem, and of branches, and likewise this whole composition, of shining gold. The leaves set on of sparkling emerald. The fruits, of their natural size, scattered here and there, with the golden rind widely split, and in the place of the seeds there burned the brightest rubies, brightest beyond any touchstone and of the thickness of a bean.

Then the ingenious maker of this inestimable work, being plentiful in his imagining, had marked off, in the place of the pith, the seeds with the thinnest silver foil. Beyond this, and reasonably, he had feigned certain other apples split open, but unripe in their seeding, where he had composed, with a bold exquisiteness, thick pearls of eastern whiteness. Skilfully too he had feigned the pomegranate flowers made of perfect coral in calyxes full of golden points.

Beyond this, out of the top of the pipe-like hollow stem there came a turning and free shaft, the lower pivot of which was fixed in a socketed head, or rather made fast upon the middle of the axle. And it rose up through the open and hollowed trunk.

Such a topmost vessel, so placed, was so perfectly wrought that when the two-wheeled carriage was moved, the shaft with the vessel joined to it turned round, spinning and pouring out the water from within the tree; and when the wheels stood still, the turning ceased. And in this way I thought that its spinning had its force from one of the wheels, which held another toothed one towards the turning spindle, which had the sockets for the teeth, and moved the stem of the vessel. The wheels were half covered by a winged work; there appeared, as it were, two spread wings, one here and the other there, adorned with certain Scyllas.

This marvellous work, running before each of us, our hands being moistened and then our faces, all made fragrant with an unthinkable scent, we rubbed our hands, so that never such nor so great a scent offered itself to my senses. And in this manner the most apt girls bestowed it.

Bedewed, then, with such a sprinkling of the most fragrant water, the mistress's servers, with a singular showing of kindness, offered a golden goblet, with which first the sovereign Queen, having with a chief affability greeted us all, drank the sweetest nectar; and thereafter in order, one with another, with reverent and gracious and mutual honourings, we solemnly drank. An excellent closing and sealing of all the favours received and of the sweet tasting.

Last of all the sweet-smelling flowers were diligently swept up, and all gathered and all the leavings carried thence away, the paving remaining bright and shining as the brightness of the most burnished mirror, rivalling the aspects standing round about and the shining gems; and, each sitting in the place appointed, the Nymph of the fountain departed.

Last of all the magnanimous and lofty Queen at once ordered an unheard-of dance, or ball, upon the jasper squares, finished with an exact artifice, burnished and bright — such a thing as among mortals was never seen nor devised.

Chapter X

The banquet. A feast of unmeasured luxury — gold and gem vessels, perfumed dishes served in order, music and dance — described course by course as a set-piece of the senses.

TANTO EXCESSO ET INCOMPARABILE gloria et triumphi, et inopinabile thesoro, et frugale delitie, et summe pompe, et solemne epulo, et lautissimo et sumptuoso Symposio, di questa foelicissima et opulentissima Regina recensito, si io distincta et perfinitamente la sua praecipua dignitate non havesse condignamente expresso, non se miravegli diciò la curiosa turbula, imperoché qualunque di acuto ingegno et expedito, et di prodiga et fertilissima lingua ornato et copioso ad questo enucleata, né coadunatamente potrebbe satisfare. Ma molto meno io che continuamente pativa per qualunque intima latebra del mio infervescente core, la indesinente pugna, quantunque absente di madona Polia, di omni mia virtute occuparia et depopulabonda praedatrice. Chiunque cogitare valeria il richo habito et exquisito ornato, et curiosissimo culto la perfecta et ambitiosa et falerata bellecia sencia alcuno defecto, la summa sapientia, la Aemiliana eloquentia, la munificentia più che regia. La praeclara dispositione di Architectura, et la obstinata Symmetria di questo aedificio perfecta et absoluta, la nobilitate dell’arte marmoraria. Poliphilo goes on to tell of an elegant dance after so great a banquet, which was a game. And how the Queen committed him to two excellent maidens of hers. Who led him to behold delicious and great things, and, talking with him, plainly instructed him upon certain doubts. At last they came to the three doors. And how he stayed at the middle door, among the amorous Nymphs.

So excessive and incomparable a glory and triumph, and unthinkable treasure, and frugal delights, and the highest pomp, and solemn feast, and most splendid and sumptuous banquet of this most happy and most opulent Queen having been recounted — if I have not distinctly and to the end worthily expressed her chief dignity, let the curious little crowd not marvel at it; for anyone of sharp and ready wit, and adorned and plentiful with a prodigal and most fertile tongue, could not satisfy this plainly, nor altogether.

But much less I, who continually suffered, in every inward hiding-place of my burning heart, the unceasing battle — however absent — of my lady Polia, the occupier and wasting plunderer of all my powers. Beyond, the many marvels, unheard of in their excellence and diversity, things unaccustomed and unlike, inestimable and not human; therefore dazzled and all alike weighed down in every sense of mine, my excessive contemplation drawn apart by the notable variety, I should not know how to describe it perfectly point by point, nor worthily to set it forth.

Who could think of the rich dress and exquisite ornament, and the most careful care; the perfect and ambitious and trapped-out beauty without any defect; the highest wisdom, the eloquence of Aemilius, the more than royal munificence. The distinguished ordering of the architecture, and the obstinate symmetry of this building, perfect and complete; the nobility of the marble-worker's art. The setting straight of the columns, the perfection of statues, the ornament of walls, the variation of stones, the royal vestibule, the most ample peristyle, the artful pavements — who would believe with what luxury and

Receiving-rooms capacious and wonderful in their art and incredible cost, with the choice praise of their most distinguished maker, every partition and elegant agreement of the distinguished lineaments deservedly approved. I beheld afterwards, with a singular pleasure, a coffered ceiling in the highest degree skilfully adorned, stretched in an even flat, without peer or comparison; it made a proud heaven, with set spacings of manifold shaping, with a drawn and levelled measure, hedging in the little areas with a noble composition, with a ready prominence, which was duly adorned with the lineament of a cornice, with little bands, gorges and egg-work, berries, or fruits of roses evenly threaded. And leaves of acanthus licking along the corners of the square and oblong little areas, with exact roses with a twinned order of foliage, the inner one smaller, with the required interval, all open, and the curved parts, in a greater relief, everything clothed, or gilded, with the best and shining gold, and with the finest and choicest dark blue colouring. With various other figurings of the ornament matching the lineament — let the beamed roof of Salauces, king of the Colchians, yield here.

Then the voluptuous pleasantness of the ordered green places and orchards, and watered gardens, living fountains, with little streams running in marble enclosures, held and hedged in with an incredible making. Grass ever fresh with dew, and flower-bearing, and sweet summer airs and spring winds with the various harmony of small birds. The pure serenity and unfailing temper of the sky, and the wholesomeness of a freest and purest air; places neither low nor stony, nor swept by constant and frosty winds, nor burnt by the unruly and scorching sun, but lit with an easy and kindly weather, and sincerely most joyful with moderation and a middle measure; the fields fertile and untilled yet fruitful of every good, sunny hills, leafy and cool little woods, pleasant with thick shade.

Afterwards the inestimable furnishing, the ready and manifold household and elegant service, the varied youth with its growing age. The most welcome presence of the girls of the hall, of the court, of the chamber, and of the royal household; the venerable and majestic sight of them, with a dress more lovely and seemly and a distinguished ornament, and with an approved and most charming comeliness, as much as ever anyone could feel or tell.

human opulence and condition — behold, then, being in this part overcome, I can conveniently conclude nothing else than that I stood senseless and out of my mind with astonishment; where I stayed with the utmost pleasure, without weariness of the things present nor with any surfeit of them. But above all, beyond what I have said, I was out of myself, turning over what fate had brought and destined me to these blessed places.

But since I found myself thus, and in so great a heaping of glory, and a holy site, and a happy country, and a blessed delight, and at the frugal and triumphing banquet — such as Clodius the tragedian never made, subject neither to the Tapullan nor the Licinian law — refreshed with a moderate fullness, and none the less by the royal promise of favouring my loving desire not vainly made secure, I comforted myself, holding as nothing all that had until now befallen me and been set in my way; and of everything I spoke well of Fortune, with a joyful gladness.

For which cause, the lofty Queen wishing to show, for a greater display beyond the things aforesaid, the excess and the surpassing of the universe in all excellent and rarest magnificences — everyone sitting in their places, after the miracle of the sumptuous banqueting, without any long delay she ordered a game to be looked at, worthy not so much of the sight as of an eternal remembrance, which also was an excellent dance, or ball, in such a course and manner.

Through the way of the curtains there entered thirty-two young girls, of whom sixteen were clothed in cloth of gold (but eight of one uniform). Then one of those sixteen clothed in gold was dressed in royal habit, and another in the dress of a Queen, with two keepers of the rock, or citadel; two silent ones, or secretaries; and two knights. With an equal number, eight were clothed in cloth of silver, with the same offices.

All these, according to their office, disposed themselves thus, placing themselves upon the squares of the pavement: that is, sixteen clothed in gold on the one side, and sixteen in silver on the other, opposite.

The musicians began to play with three instruments of daring invention, very concordant and sharing together, with a most sweet consonance and tuned melody. At the measured time of the sound, upon their squares, as the King commanded, the dancing and dolphin-like tumblers moved, and with the most seemly turnings, honouring the King and the Queen, they climbed upon the next square, making an excellent pause.

The King of the silver (the sound beginning again from the top) bade her that stood before the Queen set herself over against her. She, going forward with those same reverent gestures, made her pause and stood. In this ordered manner, according to the measuring of the musical time, thus they

loco se mutavano, o vero persistendo continuo sopra il suo quadrato ballavano dummentre che impulse, o vero prehense se partivano, cum iussione sempre del Re. Si il sono conteniva uno tempo, quelle uniforme octo consumavano quel tempo in translatarse in altro quadrato. Non poteano retrocedere, si non meritamente per havere immune salito sopra la linea delle quadratione, ove faceva residentia il Re, né rectamente procedere nisi per linea diagonale. Uno secretario et uno Equite, in uno tempo tre quadrati transivano, il Secretario per linea diagonale, lo Equite per dui aequilateri recti et uno dalla linea devio, et per omni lato poteano transferirse. Gli custodi de l’arce molti quadri rectamente valevano et licentemente trapassare. Diqué in uno tempo potevano discorrere tre, quatro, o cinque quadrati, servando la mensura, et festinante il grado. Il Re poteva ascendere sopra quale quadrato, non impedito, o vero cum praesidio occupato, anci pole prehendere, et egli interdicto il quadrato, ove altri poteno salire, et si caso egli fusse opportuno è che egli ceda cum admonitione praecedente. Ma la Regina per omni quadrato del suo colore ove primo fermoe la sedia. Et bene è che sempre propinqua segui d’ogni lato il marito suo. Qualunque fiata che gli officiali dil uno et dil altro Rege, ritrovava uno del altro sencia custodia et praesidio, il faceano pregione, et ambedue basiantise, el victo fora usciva. Per questo tale ordine feceron uno celeberrimo ludo in una Chorea elegantissima, ballando et festivamente iocando, cum la mensura del sono, per modo che ristoe vincitore quello dell’argento cum alacritate solacio et plauso. Questa tale solemne festa duroe per gli contrasti, fuge, praesidii, per tempo di una hora, cum tanto mensurate circulatione, riverentie, et pause, et modeste continentie, che tanto delectamento me invase, che io non immeritamente suspicai alle supreme delitie del summo Olympo essere rapto, et novissima foelicitate. Terminato il primo ioco in ballo, tutti al suo statuito quadrato reiterorono. Et cum il parile modo, quale feceron in prima, cusì la seconda fiata, aequalmente ad gli lochi sui ordinatamente ritornate, le sonatrice stringendo la mensura del tempo, cusì gli movimenti et gesti degli lusorii corigianti, più solicitamente se movevano, ma cum il sono servato il tempo, cum tanto aptissimo modo et approbata gesticulatione et arte, che non fue opportuno, dire alcuna cosa. Ma bene perite le damicelle, cum le sue copiose trece, sopra le delicate spalle effuse, pendevano inconstante, et poscia sopra el dorso secondo il moto resultavano, nel capo innexe cum Corolla di olente viole. Et quando una era captivata, levate le brace converberavano una palmula cum l’altra. Diqué cusì ludendo et corigiando, ristoe

changed place, or, staying always upon their square, danced while those driven forward, or taken, departed — always at the King's bidding.

If the sound held one measure, those eight of one kind used that measure in passing to another square. They could not go back, save deservedly for having climbed untouched upon the line of the squares where the King had his seat; nor go straight forward, except by a diagonal line.

A secretary and a knight passed three squares in one measure: the secretary by a diagonal line, the knight by two equal-sided straight ones and one turning off the line; and they could move to every side. The keepers of the citadel could pass straight and freely over many squares. So that in one measure they could run over three, four, or five squares, keeping the measure, and hastening their step.

The King could climb upon whatever square was not blocked, or held by a garrison — indeed he may take it; and that square is forbidden him where others may climb, and if the case be fitting he must yield, with a warning going before. But the Queen upon every square of her own colour, where she first set her seat. And it is well that she always follow her husband closely on every side.

Whenever the officers of the one or the other King found one of the other without keeping and garrison, they made him prisoner, and both kissing one another, the vanquished went out.

In this manner they made a most famous game in a most elegant dance, dancing and merrily playing with the measure of the sound, in such a way that the silver one remained the winner, with cheerfulness, solace and applause. This solemn festival lasted, by its contests, flights and garrisons, for the space of an hour, with such measured circlings, reverences and pauses, and modest stayings, that so great a delight came over me that I not undeservedly thought myself carried up to the supreme delights of the highest Olympus, and to a newest happiness.

The first game in dance being ended, all returned again to their appointed square. And in the same manner as they had done at first, so the second time, having all alike returned in order to their places, the players tightening the measure of the time, so the movements and gestures of the playing dancers moved more busily — but keeping the measure with the sound, in so most apt a manner and with so approved a gesturing and art that it was not fitting to say anything.

But the damsels were well skilled, with their plentiful tresses poured over their delicate shoulders, hanging unsteadily and then leaping upon their backs according to the movement, bound at the head with a little crown of fragrant violets. And when one was taken captive, they raised their arms and beat one palm against the other. So that, playing and dancing thus, there remained

la seconda fiata vincitore ancora il primo. Nella tertia chorea tutti ad gli lochi sui regulati et distributi, più ancora gli musici strinxeron la mensura del tempo, cum il modo et tono del excitante Phrygio, quale tonatione unque seppe ritrovare Marsyas di Phrygia. El Re vestito di oro movere fece, quella giovenetta, che inante alla Regina stava, sopra il tertio quadrato, recto incedendo nel primo trasmigrare. Per la quale cosa immediate se vide una pugna, uno torniamento, tanto delectabile, cum tanto praesta et subitanea vehementia, cum inclinarse fina in terra, facendo poscia uno repente et torculario salto, et quale Mymphurio tornatorio, cum due revolutione nel aere, una opposita ad l’altra. Et poi sencia mora, posto il pede dextro ad terra, tre fiate rotavase. Et poi subito l’altro pede, al contrario intorniava, tutta questa actione ad uno tempo consumavano, tanto accommodamente, et cum tanta agilitate che niente sopra, cum le sue profunde inclinatione et composite vertigine et facile saltatione, cum venusti gesti, quanto mai di tale et simigliante cosa se vedesse, né unque spectare se potesse, né mai tentata. Né unque l’una cum l’altra era impedimento, ma chi era apprehenso dal prehensore in instanti datogli il mostulento basio, del ioco se ne usciva, et quanto minore numero ristava, tanto più vedevase una lepidissima solertia alla deceptione di l’una all’altra. Tale digno ordine et modo da ciascuno sencia defecto fue observabile, quantunque brevemente festinata la mensuratione delle docte et praestante musice se praestasse, incitante non meno ancora ad tali movimenti tutti gli astanti, per la convenientia della consona harmonia cum l’alma maxime et praecipuamente essendo quivi in summo et concordante consenso dilla Eupathia degli dispositi corpi. Per questa tale ragione della potentia di Timotheo solertissimo musico, io caldamente pensai che egli cum el suo canto lo exercito del magno Macedonico ad reassumere l’arme violentasse, et poscia reflectendo la voce et il tono, neglecte le arme tutti cessabondi provocare. Di questo tertio ioco la vestita d’oro in forma regia gloriosamente triumphoe. Celebremente cum extrema laetitia et maximo solatio dunque terminata questa iocundissima festa, tutti se poseno ad sedere. Et quivi factomi levare, et dinanti la veneranda Sede della sua Diva maiestate feci profunda riverentia, et decentemente genuflectendome, cusì mi dixe. Poliphile horamai poni in oblivio gli praeteriti et occorsi casi, et d’indi gli fastidiosi concepti, et il transacto discrime, imperoché io son certa, che al praesente pienamente sei restaurato. Dunque volendo tu nelle amorose fiamme di Polia intrepido prosequire, convenevole cosa arbitro, che per questa recuperatione vadi ad tre porte, ove habita l’alta Regina Telosia, nel quale loco h

the winner a second time the first again.

In the third dance, all being ordered and set out in their places, the musicians tightened the measure of the time still further, with the manner and tone of the stirring Phrygian — such a sounding as Marsyas of Phrygia never knew how to find. The King clothed in gold made her that stood before the Queen move upon the third square, going straight in her first passage.

For which cause there was at once seen a battle, a tournament, so delightful, with so ready and sudden a vehemence; with bending down to the very ground, and then making a swift and twisting leap, and like a turning tumbler, with two rollings in the air, the one opposite the other. And then without delay, the right foot set to the ground, she turned round three times. And then at once with the other foot she went round the contrary way; all this action they used up in one measure, so fittingly and with so great an agility that nothing could go beyond it: with their deep bowings and ordered spinnings and easy leaping, with comely gestures, as much as ever of such and like a thing was seen, nor ever could be beheld, nor was ever attempted.

Nor was the one ever a hindrance to the other; but whoever was taken by the taker, the honeyed kiss being given her in an instant, went out of the game; and the fewer that remained, the more one saw a most charming skill in the deceiving of one by another. Such a worthy order and manner was kept by each without defect, however briefly the measuring of the learned and excellent musicians hastened it — and it stirred no less all those standing by to such movements, by the agreement of the consonant harmony with the soul, being here chiefly and above all in the highest and concordant consent of the well-being of their disposed bodies.

For this reason, of the power of Timotheus that most skilful musician, I warmly thought that he with his song forced the army of the great Macedonian to take up arms again, and then, turning back the voice and the tone, to leave their arms neglected and provoke them all to ceasing. Of this third game she that was clothed in gold in royal form gloriously triumphed.

This most joyful festival being famously ended with an extreme gladness and the greatest solace, all set themselves to sit. And here, being made to rise, and before the venerable seat of her divine majesty I made a deep reverence, and seemly kneeling, she spoke to me thus: "Poliphilo, put now into forgetfulness the past and befallen cases, and thence the wearisome thoughts, and the danger gone by, for I am certain that at present you are fully restored. Since, then, you wish to go on undaunted in the amorous flames of Polia, I judge it a fitting thing that for this recovery you should go to the three doors, where the high Queen Telosia dwells; in which place
